the fact that the person has been found guilty of an offence under this Act or the regulations, or an offence under any other Act or law,
any biosecurity audit relating to the registered entity,
any matter prescribed by the regulations,
any other circumstances that the Secretary considers relevant.
The Secretary is to give the applicant notice in writing of a decision to grant or refuse a renewal of biosecurity registration.

If the Secretary fails to give an applicant for renewal of biosecurity registration notice of a decision to grant or refuse the renewal within the period prescribed by the regulations, the Secretary is taken to have refused to renew the biosecurity registration.
Part 15 provides for accreditation audits in relation to applications.
Biosecurity registration is subject to the following conditions—
any conditions prescribed by the regulations,
any conditions imposed by the Secretary.
The Secretary may impose conditions on biosecurity registration—
at the time of the grant or renewal of biosecurity registration, or
at any other time by variation to the biosecurity registration.

A provision of this Division that authorises a type of condition to be imposed on biosecurity registration does not prevent other types of conditions being imposed, or limit the matters that can be provided for by conditions, except where expressly provided for by this Division.
In this Division—
registered entity includes a former registered entity.
The conditions of biosecurity registration may require the registered entity to engage in a registrable dealing in accordance with specified standards.

The conditions of biosecurity registration may require the registered entity to carry out specified works, or put in place specified measures, to prevent, eliminate, minimise or manage the biosecurity risk of a registrable dealing.
The conditions of biosecurity registration may require the registered entity to have in place an alternative arrangement that has been approved by the Secretary.
An alternative arrangement is a plan or arrangement relating to the registrable dealing that takes effect if—
the registered entity ceases to be authorised to engage in the registrable dealing, or
the registered entity is unable, because of illness, financial circumstances or otherwise, to continue to engage in the registrable dealing.

The conditions of biosecurity registration may require the registered entity to take out and maintain a policy of insurance that indemnifies the registered entity against any liability to which the registered entity may become subject in connection with the registrable dealing.
The conditions of biosecurity registration may require the registered entity to co-operate with, or arrange for, mandatory biosecurity audits and may provide for the frequency of biosecurity audits.

The conditions of biosecurity registration may require the registered entity to provide a financial assurance. The Secretary may require any such financial assurance to be provided before the Secretary grants, renews, varies, suspends or cancels biosecurity registration.

The purpose of a condition requiring the provision of a financial assurance is to secure or guarantee funding for or towards the doing of anything required as a result of any of the following events (each of which is a secured event)—
the registered entity contravening another condition of biosecurity registration,
the registered entity placing any biosecurity matter that registration authorises the registrable entity to deal with in the care of the Secretary,
the registered entity ceasing to be authorised to engage in the registrable dealing,
the registered entity becoming unable, because of illness, financial circumstances or otherwise, to continue to engage in the registrable dealing.
A financial assurance is not to operate as a mere penalty for a contravention of a requirement imposed by or under this Act.
A financial assurance may be in one or more of the following forms—
a bank guarantee,
a bond,
a form specified by the regulations,
another form of security that the Secretary considers appropriate and specifies in the condition.
The regulations and, subject to the regulations, the conditions of biosecurity registration, may make provision for or with respect to financial assurances, including the following—
the calculation of the amount of financial assurances that can be required,
the circumstances in which financial assurances may be claimed or realised, and the procedure for claiming or realising financial assurances,
the actions that can be taken following a secured event, including provisions that—
specify the circumstances in which those actions can be taken by or on behalf of the Secretary, and
authorise the Secretary, or a person acting on behalf of the Secretary, to enter land to carry out those actions,
the provision of information in respect of the actions,
the audit of the actions,
the administration of financial assurances,
the release of financial assurances.
The Land and Environment Court has jurisdiction to determine disputes about calling on or using a financial assurance.
A financial assurance may be called on and used, despite and without affecting—
any liability of the registered entity for any penalty for an offence for a contravention to which the assurance relates, and
any other action that might be taken or is required to be taken in relation to any contravention or other circumstances to which the assurance relates.

The conditions of biosecurity registration may provide that an authorisation conferred by the biosecurity registration does not take effect until the end of a specified period or on the happening of a particular event or on the occurrence of a specified state of affairs.

Without limiting the generality of the above, the conditions may provide that an authorisation or variation will not take effect until a financial assurance is provided in accordance with the condition.

heading.b: Suspension or cancellation of biosecurity registration
Grounds for suspension or cancellation of biosecurity registration

block.txt: Each of the following constitutes grounds for suspending or cancelling biosecurity registration—
the Secretary is of the opinion that the registered entity has contravened a requirement imposed by or under this Act,
the Secretary is of the opinion that the registered entity is not a suitable person to be involved in the registrable dealing concerned,

the Secretary receives information about the registered entity and the Secretary is of the opinion that, had the information been received at the time when the application for biosecurity registration or renewal of biosecurity registration was made, the Secretary would have refused the application,
any other grounds prescribed by the regulations.
The Secretary may also suspend or cancel biosecurity registration in the case of an emergency (in which case, the emergency is the grounds for the suspension or cancellation).
A decision about the suitability of a person to be involved in a registrable dealing may be made having regard to any of the following—
the fact that the person has been found guilty of an offence under this Act or the regulations, or an offence under any other Act or law,
a biosecurity audit,
any matter prescribed by the regulations,
any other circumstances that the Secretary considers relevant.
In this Division—
registered entity includes a former registered entity.

The Secretary may, by notice in writing to a registered entity, suspend the biosecurity registration of the registered entity if the Secretary is satisfied that there are grounds for the suspension of registration.
Notice of the suspension must specify—
the date or time from which suspension takes effect, and
the period of suspension, and
the grounds for the suspension.

heading.b: Registered entity to be given opportunity to make submissions about suspension

block.txt: Before suspending the biosecurity registration of a registered entity, the Secretary must—
give notice in writing to the registered entity of the Secretary’s intention to suspend registration and the proposed grounds for doing so, and
invite the registered entity to make a submission to the Secretary about the proposed suspension, and
take into account any submission made to the Secretary by the registered entity before the deadline for the making of a submission.

The Secretary is to specify a deadline for the making of a submission to the Secretary about a proposed suspension that is at least 30 days after notice of the proposed suspension is given to the registered entity.

The Secretary is not required to give notice under this section of a proposed suspension if the Secretary is of the opinion that the suspension is required urgently because of the biosecurity impact of the registrable dealing being carried out by the registered entity or in the case of an emergency.
However, if the Secretary suspends biosecurity registration without giving prior notice to the registered entity, the Secretary must—
give the registered entity notice in writing of the grounds for the suspension, and
invite the registered entity to make a submission to the Secretary about the suspension by a specified deadline (being at least 30 days after the notice is given to the registered entity).
If the registered entity makes a submission to the Secretary about the suspension before the specified deadline, the Secretary must—
decide whether the suspension should be revoked or continued, having regard to that submission, and
give notice in writing of that decision to the registered entity.
The Secretary may, by notice in writing to a registered entity, cancel the biosecurity registration of the registered entity if—
the Secretary is satisfied that there are grounds for the cancellation of biosecurity registration, or
the registered entity applies for cancellation of biosecurity registration.
Notice of the cancellation must specify—
the date or time from which cancellation takes effect, and
the grounds for the cancellation.

heading.b: Registered entity to be given opportunity to make submissions about cancellation

block.txt: Before cancelling the biosecurity registration of a registered entity, the Secretary must—
give notice in writing to the registered entity of the Secretary’s intention to cancel biosecurity registration and the proposed grounds for doing so, and
invite the registered entity to make a submission to the Secretary about the proposed cancellation, and
take into account any submission made to the Secretary by the registered entity before the deadline for the making of a submission.

The Secretary must specify a deadline for the making of a submission to the Secretary about the proposed cancellation that is at least 30 days after notice of the proposed cancellation is given to the registered entity.
The Secretary is not required to give notice under this section of a proposed cancellation if—
the biosecurity registration of the registered entity is suspended and either—
the registered entity was given an opportunity to make a submission about the suspension before the suspension took effect, or

the registered entity was given an opportunity to make a submission about the suspension after the suspension took effect, and the period specified by the Secretary for the making of that submission has ended, or
the registered entity has applied for cancellation of biosecurity registration.

heading.b: Effect of suspension or cancellation on conditions

block.txt: Biosecurity registration may be suspended or cancelled unconditionally or subject to such conditions as the Secretary imposes.
Those conditions may include (but are not limited to) any conditions to which the biosecurity registration was subject immediately before it was suspended or cancelled.

The Secretary may, by notice in writing given to the former registered entity, attach new conditions to, or vary or revoke any existing conditions of, the suspension or cancellation of the biosecurity registration.

heading.b: Offence of contravening condition of biosecurity registration

block.txt: A registered entity who contravenes a condition of biosecurity registration is guilty of an offence.
An offence against this section is a category 2 offence.
An offence against this section is an executive liability offence.
A person who is guilty of an offence against this section because the person contravenes a requirement of a condition of biosecurity registration to do or refrain from doing something—
continues, until the requirement is complied with and despite the fact that any specified period or time for compliance has expired or passed, to be liable to comply with the requirement, and
is guilty of a continuing offence for each day the contravention continues.
Subsection (4) does not apply to the extent that a requirement of a condition is revoked.
In this section—
registered entity includes a former registered entity.
Biosecurity registration is not transferable.
A registered entity may apply to the Secretary for a cancellation of biosecurity registration.
An application must—
be in an approved form, and
be accompanied by the fee for voluntary cancellation of biosecurity registration (if any) in respect of the dealing concerned prescribed by the regulations, and
include or be accompanied by any information or evidence required by the Secretary to assess the application.
A separate application may be required in relation to each dealing for which biosecurity registration is required.
An application for cancellation of biosecurity registration is not duly made unless it complies with this section.

heading.b: Appeal to Land and Environment Court

block.txt: A person aggrieved by any of the following decisions may appeal to the Land and Environment Court against the decision—
a decision of the Secretary to refuse biosecurity registration,
a decision of the Secretary to refuse to renew biosecurity registration,
a decision of the Secretary to suspend or cancel biosecurity registration,

a decision of the Secretary to refuse to revoke a suspension of biosecurity registration following the making of a submission by a registered entity under this Part, being a suspension of which the registered entity was not given prior notice,
a decision of the Secretary to impose any condition on biosecurity registration, or on the suspension or cancellation of biosecurity registration,
a decision of the Secretary to vary biosecurity registration.
An appeal is to be made in accordance with rules of court, but may not be made more than 28 days after the date written notice of the decision is served on the person.
Subject to any order made by the Land and Environment Court, an appeal does not operate to stay the decision to which the appeal relates.

heading.b: Biosecurity certifier may issue biosecurity certificates

block.txt: A biosecurity certifier may issue a biosecurity certificate under this Act.
A biosecurity certificate is a certificate that certifies any of the following matters—
that biosecurity matter or any other thing or area is free from, or contains a specified level of, any stated biosecurity matter (such as a specified pest, disease or contaminant),
that biosecurity matter or any other thing or area is in a specified condition,
that biosecurity matter or any other thing or area has been the subject of a specified treatment,
that biosecurity matter or any other thing or area meets specified requirements,
any matter of a kind prescribed by the regulations.
A biosecurity certificate remains in force for the period specified in the certificate.
An authorised officer who prepares a biosecurity certificate may charge the person seeking the biosecurity certificate a fee for preparing the certificate.
The fee charged is to be an amount provided for by, or calculated in accordance with, the regulations.
The fee is, for the purposes of this Act—
a recoverable amount that is payable to the Secretary, and
recoverable from the person seeking the biosecurity certificate.
See Part 20, which provides for the recovery of recoverable amounts.

Except as provided by subsections (1)–(3), the fee for the preparation of a biosecurity certificate is the fee agreed between the biosecurity certifier and the person seeking the biosecurity certificate.

A requirement imposed by or under this Act that a person obtain, or have in possession, a biosecurity certificate in relation to a matter may be satisfied by the person obtaining, or having in possession, an interstate biosecurity certificate in relation to that matter that is in force.

An interstate biosecurity certificate is a certificate or other document duly issued under a corresponding law in which a person certifies any matter in relation to which a biosecurity certificate could be issued under this Act and that is in force.

heading.b: Provision of false or misleading information to biosecurity certifier

block.txt: A person who, in connection with obtaining or the issue of a biosecurity certificate, furnishes any information to a biosecurity certifier that is false or misleading in a material particular, or fails to furnish any material information, is guilty of an offence.
An offence against this section is a category 1 offence if the offence is committed intentionally or recklessly.
In any other case, the offence is a category 2 offence.
A category 1 offence or category 2 offence against this section is an executive liability offence.
In this section—
biosecurity certifier includes an identified individual with respect to the issuing of biosecurity certificates by a biosecurity certifier.
A person who issues, or purports to issue, a biosecurity certificate or purported biosecurity certificate is guilty of an offence if the certificate is false or misleading in a material particular.

A person who alters or amends a biosecurity certificate, or purported biosecurity certificate, is guilty of an offence if the alteration or amendment makes the certificate false or misleading in a material particular.
A certificate is false or misleading in a material particular if it—
includes information that is false or misleading in a material particular, or
omits material information.
An offence against subsection (1) or (2) is a category 1 offence if the offence is committed intentionally or recklessly.
In any other case, an offence against subsection (1) or (2) is a category 2 offence.
A category 1 offence or category 2 offence against subsection (1) or (2) is an executive liability offence.
In this section—
biosecurity certificate includes an interstate biosecurity certificate.
A person who falsely represents that a biosecurity certificate has been issued in respect of any matter is guilty of an offence.
An offence against this section is a category 1 offence if the offence is committed intentionally or recklessly.
In any other case, an offence against this section is a category 2 offence.
A category 1 offence or category 2 offence against this section is an executive liability offence.
In this section—
biosecurity certificate includes an interstate biosecurity certificate.

heading.b: Issue or alteration of biosecurity certificate by unauthorised person

block.txt: A person who issues, or purports to issue, a biosecurity certificate or purported biosecurity certificate is guilty of an offence if the person is not a biosecurity certifier, or an identified individual with respect to the issuing of biosecurity certificates by a biosecurity certifier, authorised by or under this Act to issue the certificate concerned.

A person who alters or amends a biosecurity certificate, or purported biosecurity certificate, is guilty of an offence unless the person is a biosecurity certifier, or an identified individual with respect to the issuing of biosecurity certificates by a biosecurity certifier, authorised by or under this Act to do so.
An offence against subsection (1) or (2) is a category 1 offence if the offence is committed intentionally or recklessly.
In any other case, an offence against subsection (1) or (2) is a category 2 offence.
A category 1 offence or category 2 offence against this section is an executive liability offence.

heading.b: Grant of accreditation by accreditation authority

block.txt: An accreditation authority may, by instrument in writing, grant accreditation as a biosecurity certifier to any person, subject to this Act.
An accreditation authority is required to adopt an accreditation policy for the purposes of this Act.
An accreditation policy may make provision for or with respect to the following matters—
the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required with respect to the issue of biosecurity certificates by biosecurity certifiers accredited by the accreditation authority,
the suitability of individuals to carry out the function of issuing biosecurity certificates for biosecurity certifiers accredited by the accreditation authority,
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
An accreditation authority is to make the accreditation policy publicly available.
An accreditation policy adopted by an accreditation authority (other than the Secretary) has no effect unless it has been approved by the Secretary.
An accreditation authority may amend or replace an accreditation policy adopted by the accreditation authority.
Subsection (4) applies in relation to the amendment or replacement of an accreditation policy in the same way as it applies to the adoption of an accreditation policy.
However, subsection (4) does not apply to an amendment of an accreditation policy if the accreditation authority certifies that the amendment—
is minor in nature or for the purpose of correcting an error, or
is necessary to reflect a change of a course (including a continuing professional development course) or qualification or of the provider of a course or qualification.
An accreditation authority may adopt different accreditation policies for different types of accreditation.

A reference in this Act to an accreditation authority’s accreditation policy is a reference to the accreditation policy as adopted by the accreditation authority, being, if the authority has more than one policy, the accreditation policy that is relevant to the type of accreditation concerned.
Accreditation as a biosecurity certifier authorises the biosecurity certifier to issue biosecurity certificates.
The authorisation is subject to any conditions or limitations specified in the instrument by which the person is accredited as a biosecurity certifier.
In particular, an accreditation may be limited to—
a specified class of biosecurity certificates, or
the certification, by the issue of a biosecurity certificate, of specified matters.
Nothing in this Act authorises or requires a biosecurity certifier to act in contravention of the conditions or limitations of the biosecurity certifier’s accreditation as a biosecurity certifier.
An accreditation authority that grants accreditation to a person as a biosecurity certifier is the responsible accreditation authority in relation to that accreditation.

An accreditation authority ceases to be the responsible accreditation authority in relation to an accreditation if the accreditation is renewed by another accreditation authority. In that case, the accreditation authority that renews the accreditation becomes the responsible accreditation authority in relation to the accreditation.

The Secretary is entitled, but is not required, to exercise any of the functions of the responsible accreditation authority in relation to an accreditation granted or renewed by an accreditation authority.

If an accreditation authority ceases to be an accreditation authority in relation to accreditation generally or a class of accreditation, the functions of the responsible accreditation authority in relation to any accreditation, or accreditation of that class, that has already been granted or renewed by that accreditation authority may be exercised by—
any accreditation authority approved by the Secretary to exercise the functions of the accreditation authority in respect of the accreditation or class of accreditation concerned, or
if no accreditation authority has been so approved, the Secretary.

heading.b: Approval of authorised officer to exercise functions of biosecurity certifier

block.txt: The Secretary may, by instrument in writing, approve any authorised officer to exercise any specified function or functions of a biosecurity certifier.
An approval may apply to a specified authorised officer or to any specified class of authorised officers.
An approval may be unconditional, or subject to conditions or limitations.
An approval has effect for the period specified in the instrument of approval or, if no period is specified, until revoked by the Secretary.
The Secretary may, by instrument in writing, revoke or amend an approval under this section at any time.
The approval of a person as a biosecurity certifier under this section ceases to be in force if the person ceases to be an authorised officer.
A person approved to exercise the functions of a biosecurity certifier under this section is taken to be a biosecurity certifier.
Nothing in this Act authorises or requires the person to act in contravention of the conditions or limitations of his or her approval to exercise the functions of a biosecurity certifier.
A person may apply to an accreditation authority for accreditation as a biosecurity certifier.
An application must—
be in a form approved by the accreditation authority, and
include or be accompanied by any information or evidence of a kind prescribed by the regulations, and
include or be accompanied by any other information or evidence that the accreditation authority reasonably requires to assess the application.
The accreditation authority may require a fee to be paid for an application for accreditation.
The accreditation authority may require the application fee to accompany the application.
The amount of the application fee is—
if the accreditation authority is the Secretary—the amount provided for by the regulations, or
in any other case—the amount required by the accreditation authority.
The accreditation authority may, on application, grant or refuse to grant accreditation as a biosecurity certifier.
The accreditation authority may refuse to grant accreditation—
if the application for accreditation does not comply with any requirement imposed by or under this Act, or

if the accreditation authority is not satisfied that the applicant can ensure that the issue of biosecurity certificates by the applicant will be carried out only by individuals who are suitable and have the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required by the accreditation authority’s accreditation policy, or
if the accreditation authority is of the opinion that the applicant is not a suitable person to be accredited as a biosecurity certifier, or
on any grounds prescribed by the regulations.
A decision about the suitability of a person for accreditation may be made having regard to any of the following—
the fact that the applicant has been found guilty of an offence under this Act or the regulations, or an offence under any other Act or law,
an accreditation audit,
any matter prescribed by the regulations,
any other circumstances that the accreditation authority considers relevant.
The regulations may prescribe circumstances in which it is mandatory for an accreditation authority to refuse accreditation.
An accreditation authority must refuse accreditation if it is mandatory for the accreditation authority to refuse accreditation.
The accreditation authority is to give the applicant notice in writing of a decision to grant or refuse accreditation.

An accreditation authority that fails to give an applicant for accreditation notice of a decision to grant or refuse accreditation within the period prescribed by the regulations is taken to have refused accreditation.
Accreditation remains in force for a period (not exceeding 5 years) specified by the accreditation authority in any notice by which accreditation is granted or renewed, unless sooner cancelled.
Accreditation has no effect during any period in which accreditation is suspended.

The responsible accreditation authority may, at any time, by notice in writing to a person who has been accredited as a biosecurity certifier, vary the accreditation of the person (including any conditions of accreditation imposed by an accreditation authority).
A variation includes the imposition of new conditions on accreditation, the substitution of a condition, or the omission or amendment of a condition.
The regulations may make further provision for the variation of accreditation, including—
applications for variation, and
fees for applications for variation.
A biosecurity certifier may apply to an accreditation authority for renewal of accreditation as a biosecurity certifier.
An application must—
be in a form approved by the accreditation authority, and
include or be accompanied by any information or evidence of a kind prescribed by the regulations, and
include or be accompanied by any other information or evidence that the accreditation authority reasonably requires to assess the application.
The accreditation authority may require a fee to be paid for an application for renewal of accreditation.
The accreditation authority may require the application fee to accompany the application.
The amount of the application fee is—
if the accreditation authority is the Secretary—the amount provided for by the regulations, or
in any other case—the amount required by the accreditation authority.

If an application for renewal of accreditation is duly made to an accreditation authority before the expiry of accreditation, accreditation is taken to continue in force until the accreditation authority notifies the applicant of a decision to grant or refuse the application.

heading.b: Grant or refusal of renewal application

block.txt: An accreditation authority may, on application, renew or refuse to renew accreditation as a biosecurity certifier.
An accreditation authority may refuse to renew accreditation—
if the application for renewal of accreditation does not comply with any requirement imposed by or under this Act, or

if the accreditation authority is not satisfied that the applicant can ensure that the issue of biosecurity certificates by the applicant will be carried out only by individuals who are suitable and have the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required by the accreditation authority’s accreditation policy, or
if the accreditation authority is of the opinion that the applicant is not a suitable person to be accredited as a biosecurity certifier, or
on any grounds prescribed by the regulations.
A decision about the suitability of a person for accreditation may be made having regard to any of the following—
the fact that the applicant has been found guilty of an offence under this Act or the regulations, or an offence under any other Act or law,
any biosecurity audit relating to the biosecurity certifier,
any matter prescribed by the regulations,
any other circumstances that the accreditation authority considers relevant.
The regulations may prescribe circumstances in which it is mandatory for an accreditation authority to refuse to renew accreditation.
An accreditation authority must refuse to renew accreditation if it is mandatory for the accreditation authority to refuse to renew accreditation.
An accreditation authority is to give the applicant notice in writing of a decision to grant or refuse renewal of accreditation.

An accreditation authority that fails to give an applicant for accreditation notice of a decision to grant or refuse the renewal of accreditation within the period prescribed by the regulations is taken to have refused accreditation.
Accreditation as a biosecurity certifier is subject to the following conditions—
any conditions prescribed by the regulations,
any conditions imposed by the responsible accreditation authority.
The responsible accreditation authority may impose conditions on accreditation—
at the time of the grant or renewal of accreditation, or
at any other time by variation to the accreditation.

A provision of this Part that authorises a type of condition to be imposed on accreditation does not prevent other types of conditions being imposed or limit the matters that can be provided for by conditions, except where expressly provided for by this Part.
The conditions of accreditation may require the biosecurity certifier to exercise the functions of a biosecurity certifier in accordance with specified standards.

The conditions of accreditation may require the biosecurity certifier to take out and maintain a policy of insurance that indemnifies the biosecurity certifier for any liability to which the biosecurity certifier may become subject as a result of exercising, or purporting to exercise, the functions of a biosecurity certifier.

heading.b: Condition that work be carried out only by individuals

block.txt: It is a condition of the accreditation of a biosecurity certifier that the issue of biosecurity certificates by the biosecurity certifier will be carried out only by an individual—
with the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required by the responsible accreditation authority’s accreditation policy, and
who is the biosecurity certifier or who is an identified individual with respect to the issuing of biosecurity certificates for the biosecurity certifier.

heading.b: Grounds for suspension or cancellation of accreditation

block.txt: Each of the following constitutes grounds for suspending or cancelling accreditation as a biosecurity certifier—
the accreditation authority is of the opinion that the biosecurity certifier has contravened a requirement imposed by or under this Act,

the accreditation authority is not satisfied that the biosecurity certifier can ensure that the issue of biosecurity certificates by the biosecurity certifier will be carried out only by individuals who are suitable and have the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required by the accreditation authority’s accreditation policy,
the accreditation authority is of the opinion that the biosecurity certifier is not a suitable person to be accredited as a biosecurity certifier,

the accreditation authority receives information about the biosecurity certifier and the accreditation authority is of the opinion that, had the information been received at the time when the application for accreditation or renewal of accreditation was made, it would have refused the application,
any other grounds prescribed by the regulations.
A decision about the suitability of a person for accreditation may be made having regard to any of the following—
the fact that the biosecurity certifier has been found guilty of an offence under this Act or the regulations, or an offence under any other Act or law,
a biosecurity audit relating to the biosecurity certifier,
any matter prescribed by the regulations,
any other circumstances that the accreditation authority considers relevant.
In this Division—
biosecurity certifier includes a former biosecurity certifier.

The responsible accreditation authority may, by notice in writing to a biosecurity certifier, suspend the accreditation of the biosecurity certifier if the accreditation authority is satisfied that there are grounds for the suspension of accreditation.
The regulations may prescribe circumstances in which it is mandatory for the responsible accreditation authority to suspend the accreditation of a biosecurity certifier.
A responsible accreditation authority must suspend the accreditation of a biosecurity certifier if it is mandatory for the accreditation authority to suspend the accreditation.
Notice of the suspension must specify—
the date or time from which suspension takes effect, and
the period of suspension, and
the grounds for the suspension.

heading.b: Biosecurity certifier to be given opportunity to make submissions about suspension

block.txt: Before suspending the accreditation of a biosecurity certifier, an accreditation authority must—
give notice in writing to the biosecurity certifier of the accreditation authority’s intention to suspend accreditation and the proposed grounds for doing so, and
invite the biosecurity certifier to make a submission to the accreditation authority about the proposed suspension, and
take into account any submission made to the accreditation authority by the biosecurity certifier before the deadline for the making of a submission.

An accreditation authority is to specify a deadline for the making of a submission to the accreditation authority about the proposed suspension that is at least 30 days after the notice of the proposed suspension is given to the biosecurity certifier.

An accreditation authority is not required to give notice under this section of a proposed suspension if the accreditation authority proposes to suspend the accreditation because the accreditation authority is of the opinion that—
the suspension relates to a matter of critical non-compliance, or
the biosecurity certifier has issued a biosecurity certificate that is false or misleading in a material particular or has otherwise engaged in fraudulent behaviour.
However, if the accreditation authority suspends accreditation of a biosecurity certifier without giving prior notice to the biosecurity certifier, the accreditation authority must—
give the biosecurity certifier notice in writing of the grounds for the suspension, and

invite the biosecurity certifier to make a submission to the accreditation authority about the suspension by a specified deadline that is at least 30 days after the notice is given to the biosecurity certifier.
If the biosecurity certifier makes a submission to the accreditation authority about the suspension before the specified deadline, the accreditation authority must—
decide whether the suspension should be revoked or continued, having regard to that submission, and
give notice in writing of that decision to the biosecurity certifier.
The responsible accreditation authority may, by notice in writing to a biosecurity certifier, cancel the accreditation of the biosecurity certifier if—
there are grounds for the cancellation of accreditation, or
the biosecurity certifier applies for cancellation of accreditation.
The regulations may prescribe circumstances in which it is mandatory for the responsible accreditation authority to cancel the accreditation of a biosecurity certifier.
A responsible accreditation authority must cancel the accreditation of a biosecurity certifier if it is mandatory for the accreditation authority to cancel the accreditation.
Notice of the cancellation must specify—
the date or time from which cancellation takes effect, and
the grounds for the cancellation.

heading.b: Biosecurity certifier to be given opportunity to make submissions about cancellation

block.txt: Before cancelling the accreditation of a biosecurity certifier, an accreditation authority must—
give notice in writing to the biosecurity certifier of the accreditation authority’s intention to cancel accreditation and the proposed grounds for doing so, and
invite the biosecurity certifier to make a submission to the accreditation authority about the proposed cancellation, and
take into account any submission made to the accreditation authority by the biosecurity certifier before the deadline for the making of a submission.

An accreditation authority must specify a deadline for the making of a submission to the accreditation authority about the proposed cancellation that is at least 30 days after the notice of the proposed cancellation is given to the biosecurity certifier.
An accreditation authority is not required to give notice under this section of a proposed cancellation if—
the accreditation of the biosecurity certifier is suspended and either—
the biosecurity certifier was given an opportunity to make a submission about the suspension before the suspension took effect, or

the biosecurity certifier was given an opportunity to make a submission about the suspension after the suspension took effect, and the period specified by the accreditation authority for the making of that submission has ended, or
the biosecurity certifier has applied for cancellation of accreditation.

heading.b: Effect of suspension or cancellation on conditions

block.txt: Accreditation may be suspended or cancelled unconditionally or subject to such conditions as the accreditation authority imposes.
Those conditions may include (but are not limited to) any conditions to which the accreditation was subject immediately before it was suspended or cancelled.

The accreditation authority may, by notice in writing given to the former biosecurity certifier, attach new conditions to, or vary or revoke any existing conditions of, the suspension or cancellation of the accreditation.

heading.b: Offence of contravening conditions of accreditation

block.txt: A biosecurity certifier or former biosecurity certifier who contravenes a condition of accreditation imposed by or under this Part is guilty of an offence.
An offence against this section is a category 2 offence.
An offence against this section is an executive liability offence.
A person who is guilty of an offence against this section because the person contravenes a requirement of a condition of accreditation to do or refrain from doing something—
continues, until the requirement is complied with and despite the fact that any specified period or time for compliance has expired or passed, to be liable to comply with the requirement, and
is guilty of a continuing offence for each day the contravention continues.
Subsection (3) does not apply to the extent that a requirement of a condition is revoked.
A person who impersonates a biosecurity certifier is guilty of an offence.
An offence against this section is a category 2 offence.
In this section—
biosecurity certifier includes a person who is accredited or otherwise authorised by or under a corresponding law to issue, alter or amend an interstate biosecurity certificate.

heading.b: Appeal to Land and Environment Court

block.txt: A person aggrieved by any of the following decisions may appeal to the Land and Environment Court against the decision—
a decision of an accreditation authority to refuse accreditation,
a decision of an accreditation authority to refuse to renew accreditation,
a decision of an accreditation authority to suspend or cancel accreditation,

a decision of an accreditation authority to refuse to revoke a suspension of accreditation following the making of a submission by the biosecurity certifier under this Part, being a suspension of which the biosecurity certifier was not given prior notice,
a decision of an accreditation authority to impose any condition on accreditation, or on the suspension or cancellation of accreditation,
a decision of an accreditation authority to vary accreditation.
An appeal is to be made in accordance with rules of court, but may not be made more than 28 days after the date written notice of the decision is served on the person.
Subject to any order made by the Land and Environment Court, an appeal does not operate to stay the decision to which the appeal relates.
The following types of audit (each of which is a biosecurity audit) may be conducted under this Act—
an accreditation audit,
a compliance audit.

heading.b: Audits to be conducted by biosecurity auditor only

block.txt: A biosecurity audit may be conducted only by a biosecurity auditor.
A biosecurity audit is mandatory when required by the Secretary or an accreditation authority under this Act.
In this Part, the audit target is the person the subject of a biosecurity audit.
An accreditation audit is an audit that is conducted for the purposes of assessing—
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, biosecurity registration, or
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, accreditation as a biosecurity certifier, or
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, appointment as a biosecurity auditor, or
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, a permit, or
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, approval to exercise any of the functions of an accreditation authority under this Act.
The Secretary may require an accreditation audit to be conducted in relation to any of the following applications—
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, biosecurity registration,
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, a permit,
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, approval to exercise any of the functions of an accreditation authority under this Act.
An accreditation authority may require an accreditation audit to be conducted in relation to any of the following applications—
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, accreditation as a biosecurity certifier that is made to the accreditation authority,
an application for the grant or renewal of, or variation to, appointment as a biosecurity auditor that is made to the accreditation authority.
An accreditation authority, other than the Secretary, must require an accreditation audit to be conducted in relation to an application if—
it is directed to do so by the Secretary, or
it is required to do so under the conditions of its approval as an accreditation authority.
A person who requires an accreditation audit is to give the audit target notice in writing of the decision to require an accreditation audit.
A reference in this Division to the person who requires an accreditation audit is a reference to the person who requires the accreditation audit under the power conferred by this section.
A person who requires an accreditation audit may—
engage a biosecurity auditor to conduct the audit, or
direct the audit target to engage a biosecurity auditor to conduct the audit.

If the person who requires the accreditation audit directs the audit target to engage a biosecurity auditor to conduct the audit, the person may specify requirements relating to the engagement of the biosecurity auditor and the scope of the accreditation audit.

heading.b: Functions of biosecurity auditor in relation to accreditation audit

block.txt: A biosecurity auditor has the following functions in connection with an accreditation audit, subject to any limitations specified in the biosecurity auditor’s instrument of engagement—

to assess the audit target’s suitability for the grant, renewal or variation of biosecurity registration, accreditation as a biosecurity certifier, appointment as a biosecurity auditor, a permit or approval as an accreditation authority (as the case requires),

to assess whether the audit target has the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience (if any) required for biosecurity registration, accreditation as a biosecurity certifier, appointment as a biosecurity auditor, a permit or approval as an accreditation authority (as the case requires),
to assess the audit target’s compliance with, and capability of complying with, the requirements imposed or proposed to be imposed by or under this Act,
to report to the person who requires the accreditation audit on the biosecurity auditor’s assessment of those matters.

A biosecurity auditor has such other functions in connection with an accreditation audit as are prescribed by the regulations or, subject to the regulations, conferred on the biosecurity auditor by the biosecurity auditor’s instrument of engagement.

heading.b: Recovery of fee for accreditation audit

block.txt: A person who requires an accreditation audit may charge the audit target a reasonable fee for the conduct of an accreditation audit by a biosecurity auditor engaged by the person.
If the person who requires the accreditation audit is the Secretary, the fee—
is a recoverable amount that is payable to the Secretary, and
is recoverable from the audit target.
See Part 20, which provides for the recovery of recoverable amounts.

If the person who requires the accreditation audit is an accreditation authority (other than the Secretary), the fee is recoverable by the accreditation authority as a debt in a court of competent jurisdiction.
An audit target is responsible for any fee payable in connection with an accreditation audit conducted by a biosecurity auditor engaged by the audit target.
A person who requires an accreditation audit is to have regard to that accreditation audit in exercising the person’s functions under this Act in relation to the audit target.
A compliance audit is an audit that is conducted for any of the following purposes—
to assess compliance with, and capability of complying with, the requirements imposed by or under this Act,

to assess or identify any contravention or suspected contravention of the requirements imposed by or under this Act (including any contravention or other deficiency identified in another biosecurity audit),
to identify measures for improved compliance with the requirements imposed by or under this Act.
The Secretary may require a compliance audit to be conducted in relation to any person at any time.

An accreditation authority, other than the Secretary, may require a compliance audit to be conducted in relation to a person who is or was formerly a biosecurity certifier or biosecurity auditor at any time, but only if the accreditation authority is the responsible accreditation authority for the accreditation or appointment of the person.

A person who requires a compliance audit to be conducted is to give the audit target notice of the decision to require a compliance audit, unless the giving of notice would defeat the purpose of the audit.

A reference in this Division to the person who requires, or can require, a compliance audit is a reference to the person who requires, or who has power to require, the compliance audit under the power conferred by this section.
A person who can require a compliance audit must, in making a decision about whether to require the compliance audit, or the frequency of compliance audits, have regard to the following—
the person’s audit frequency policy,
the compliance history of the audit target,
any previous biosecurity audits conducted in relation to the audit target that the person considers relevant (including any deficiencies identified in those audits),
any information provided to the person by authorised officers about compliance with requirements imposed by or under this Act,
any other matters the person considers relevant.
An accreditation authority (other than the Secretary) must require a compliance audit to be conducted in relation to a person if—
it is directed to do so by the Secretary, or
it is required to do so under the conditions of its approval as an accreditation authority.
Subsection (1) applies to a decision of the Secretary to direct an accreditation authority to require a compliance audit as if the Secretary were requiring the compliance audit.
A person who can require a compliance audit is required to adopt an audit frequency policy for the purposes of this Act.
An audit frequency policy may make provision for or with respect to the following matters—
the frequency of compliance audits,
any other matters that are prescribed by the regulations.
An audit frequency policy adopted by a person who can require a compliance audit (other than the Secretary) has no effect unless it has been approved in writing by the Secretary.
A person may amend or replace an audit frequency policy adopted by the person.
Subsection (3) applies in relation to the amendment or replacement of an audit frequency policy in the same way as it applies to the adoption of an audit frequency policy.

However, subsection (3) does not apply to an amendment of an audit frequency policy if the person making the amendment certifies that the amendment is minor in nature or for the purpose of correcting an error.
An audit frequency policy may apply generally or apply differently according to different factors of a specified kind, such as the following—
the type of biosecurity matter involved,
the type of activity involved and the level of biosecurity risk associated with that activity,
the class of biosecurity registration or accreditation involved (if any).
A person who can require a compliance audit is to make the person’s audit frequency policy publicly available.

A reference in this Act to a person’s audit frequency policy is a reference to the audit frequency policy adopted by the person or, if the person has more than one policy, the audit frequency policy that is relevant to the audit concerned.
A person who requires a compliance audit may—
engage a biosecurity auditor to conduct the audit, or
direct the audit target to engage a biosecurity auditor to conduct the audit.
The person who requires the compliance audit may direct the audit target to engage a biosecurity auditor to conduct an audit only if the audit target is a biosecurity participant.

If the person who requires the compliance audit to be conducted directs the audit target to engage a biosecurity auditor to conduct the audit, the person may specify requirements relating to the engagement of the biosecurity auditor and the scope of the compliance audit.

heading.b: Functions of biosecurity auditor in relation to compliance audit

block.txt: A biosecurity auditor has the following functions in connection with a compliance audit, subject to any limitations specified in the biosecurity auditor’s instrument of engagement—
to assess the audit target’s compliance with, and capability of complying with, the requirements imposed by or under this Act,

to assess or identify any contravention or suspected contravention of the requirements imposed by or under this Act (including any contravention or other deficiency identified in another biosecurity audit),
to identify measures for improved compliance with the requirements imposed by or under this Act,
to report to the person who requires the audit on the biosecurity auditor’s assessment of those matters.

A biosecurity auditor has such other functions in connection with a compliance audit as are prescribed by the regulations or, subject to the regulations, conferred on the biosecurity auditor by the biosecurity auditor’s instrument of engagement.

heading.b: Recovery of fee for compliance audit

block.txt: A person who requires a compliance audit may charge the audit target a reasonable fee for the conduct of a compliance audit by a biosecurity auditor engaged by the person, but only if the audit target is a biosecurity participant.
If the person who requires the compliance audit is the Secretary, the fee—
is a recoverable amount that is payable to the Secretary, and
is recoverable from the audit target.
See Part 20, which provides for the recovery of recoverable amounts.

If the person who requires the compliance audit is an accreditation authority (other than the Secretary), the fee is recoverable by the accreditation authority as a debt in a court of competent jurisdiction.
An audit target is responsible for any fee payable in connection with a compliance audit conducted by a biosecurity auditor engaged by the audit target.
A person who requires a compliance audit is to have regard to that compliance audit in exercising the person’s functions under this Act in relation to the audit target.
A biosecurity auditor has the following functions—
conducting biosecurity audits,
any other functions conferred by or under this Act.
A biosecurity auditor who is an authorised officer may exercise his or her functions as a biosecurity auditor on premises entered under Part 8.

A biosecurity auditor who is not an authorised officer may accompany an authorised officer who enters premises under Part 8 for the purpose of exercising the biosecurity auditor’s functions as a biosecurity auditor.
This section does not prevent a biosecurity auditor from—
entering or remaining on any premises, or doing anything else on premises, with the consent of the occupier of the premises, or
entering or remaining in any public place while that place is open to the public.

Failure to consent to entry by a biosecurity auditor, or to co-operate with a biosecurity audit, may constitute a contravention of conditions of biosecurity registration, a permit, accreditation as a biosecurity certifier, appointment as a biosecurity auditor or approval as an accreditation authority.
In this section—
biosecurity auditor includes an individual who is an identified individual with respect to any function of a biosecurity auditor.

A biosecurity auditor exercising a function conferred by or under this Act may exercise the function with the assistance of such other persons as the biosecurity auditor considers necessary, subject to any conditions of appointment as a biosecurity auditor.
A biosecurity auditor must prepare a written report about each biosecurity audit.
A copy of the report must be submitted—
to the person who required the audit to be conducted, and
to the audit target.
The report must be submitted within 21 days after completion of the biosecurity audit or, if another period is prescribed by the regulations, within the prescribed period.
The report must indicate the biosecurity auditor’s opinion as to the following—
whether or not the audit target is complying, and capable of complying, with the requirements imposed by or under this Act,
the requirements imposed by or under this Act that the audit target is not complying with or not capable of complying with,
if the biosecurity audit indicates contraventions of the requirements imposed by or under this Act or other deficiencies—
the nature of those contraventions or other deficiencies, and
the actions that are required to remedy those contraventions or deficiencies,
if a previous biosecurity audit has indicated contraventions or other deficiencies, the actions (if any) that have been taken to remedy those contraventions or other deficiencies.
An accreditation authority must provide to the Secretary a copy of the report submitted to the accreditation authority if directed to do so by the Secretary.
The regulations may require further matters to be included in the report.

heading.b: Certain matters to be reported immediately

block.txt: A biosecurity auditor must report to the Secretary if, during a biosecurity audit, the biosecurity auditor becomes aware of, or suspects, any of the following occurrences—
any instance of critical non-compliance by the audit target,
that a biosecurity certificate has been issued that is false or misleading in a material particular,
that a person is in possession of biosecurity matter in contravention of a requirement imposed by or under this Act,
any occurrence of a kind prescribed by the regulations.
The report must be given orally to the Secretary as soon as possible but in any case within 24 hours after the biosecurity auditor becomes aware of the matter.
A biosecurity auditor must give the Secretary a copy of the report in writing within 5 days of becoming aware of the matter.
The requirement imposed by this section is taken to be a condition of appointment as a biosecurity auditor.
A person who obstructs or hinders a biosecurity auditor in the exercise of the biosecurity auditor’s functions under this Act is guilty of an offence.
An offence against subsection (1) is a category 2 offence.
A person does not obstruct or hinder a biosecurity auditor by refusing permission to enter or remain on premises, unless—
the biosecurity auditor has the power under this Act to enter and remain on those premises because the biosecurity auditor is an authorised officer or is in the company of an authorised officer, or
the biosecurity auditor enters the premises under the power conferred by a search warrant.

However, any such refusal may constitute a contravention of the conditions of biosecurity registration, a permit, accreditation as a biosecurity certifier, appointment as a biosecurity auditor or approval as an accreditation authority.
In this section—
biosecurity auditor includes an individual who is an identified individual with respect to any function of a biosecurity auditor.

heading.b: Provision of false or misleading information to biosecurity auditor

block.txt: A person who, in connection with a biosecurity audit, furnishes any information to a biosecurity auditor that the person knows to be false or misleading in a material particular is guilty of an offence.
An offence against this section is a category 2 offence.
In this section—
biosecurity auditor includes an individual who is an identified individual with respect to the conduct of biosecurity audits by a biosecurity auditor.

heading.b: Appointment of auditors by accreditation authority

block.txt: An accreditation authority may, by instrument in writing, appoint any person as a biosecurity auditor, subject to this Act.
An accreditation authority that has the power to appoint biosecurity auditors is required to adopt an appointment policy for the purposes of this Act.
An appointment policy may make provision for or with respect to the following matters—
the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required with respect to the conduct of biosecurity audits by biosecurity auditors appointed by the accreditation authority,
the suitability of individuals to carry out the function of conducting biosecurity audits for biosecurity auditors appointed by the accreditation authority,
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
An accreditation authority is to make the appointment policy publicly available.
An appointment policy adopted by an accreditation authority (other than the Secretary) has no effect unless it has been approved by the Secretary.
An accreditation authority may amend or replace an appointment policy adopted by the accreditation authority.
Subsection (4) applies in relation to the amendment or replacement of an appointment policy in the same way as it applies to the adoption of an appointment policy.
However, subsection (4) does not apply to an amendment of an appointment policy if the accreditation authority certifies that the amendment—
is minor in nature or for the purpose of correcting an error, or
is necessary to reflect a change of a course (including a continuing professional development course) or qualification or of the provider of a course or qualification.
An accreditation authority may adopt different appointment policies for different types of biosecurity auditors or biosecurity audits.

A reference in this Act to an accreditation authority’s appointment policy is a reference to the appointment policy as adopted by the accreditation authority, being, if the authority has more than one policy, the appointment policy that is relevant to the appointment or type of appointment concerned.
Appointment as a biosecurity auditor authorises the biosecurity auditor to conduct biosecurity audits.
The authorisation is subject to any conditions or limitations specified in the biosecurity auditor’s instrument of appointment.
In particular, the authorisation may be limited to a specified class of biosecurity audit.
Nothing in this Act authorises or requires a biosecurity auditor to act in contravention of the conditions or limitations of the biosecurity auditor’s appointment as a biosecurity auditor.
An accreditation authority that appoints a person as a biosecurity auditor is the responsible accreditation authority in relation to that appointment.

An accreditation authority ceases to be the responsible accreditation authority in relation to an appointment if the appointment is renewed by another accreditation authority. In that case, the accreditation authority that renews the appointment becomes the responsible accreditation authority in relation to the appointment.

The Secretary is entitled, but is not required, to exercise any of the functions of the responsible accreditation authority in relation to an appointment granted or renewed by an accreditation authority.

If an accreditation authority ceases to be an accreditation authority in relation to appointments generally or any class of appointments, the functions of the responsible accreditation authority in relation to any appointment or class of appointments that has already been granted or renewed by that accreditation authority may be exercised by—
any accreditation authority approved by the Secretary to exercise the functions of the accreditation authority in respect of the appointment or class of appointments concerned, or
if no accreditation authority has been so approved, the Secretary.

heading.b: Approval of authorised officer to exercise functions of biosecurity auditor

block.txt: The Secretary may, by instrument in writing, approve any authorised officer to exercise any specified function or functions of a biosecurity auditor.
An approval may apply to a specified authorised officer or to any specified class of authorised officers.
An approval may be unconditional, or subject to conditions or limitations.
An approval has effect for the period specified in the instrument of approval or, if no period is specified, until revoked by the Secretary.
The Secretary may, by instrument in writing, revoke or amend an approval under this section at any time.
The approval of a person as a biosecurity auditor under this section ceases to be in force if the person ceases to be an authorised officer.
A person approved to exercise the functions of a biosecurity auditor under this section is taken to be a biosecurity auditor.
Nothing in this Act authorises or requires the person to act in contravention of the conditions or limitations of his or her approval to exercise the functions of a biosecurity auditor.
A person may apply to an accreditation authority for appointment as a biosecurity auditor.
An application must—
be in a form approved by the accreditation authority, and
include or be accompanied by any information or evidence of a kind prescribed by the regulations, and
include or be accompanied by any other information or evidence that the accreditation authority reasonably requires to assess the application.
The accreditation authority may require a fee to be paid for an application for appointment.
The accreditation authority may require the application fee to accompany the application.
The amount of the application fee is—
if the accreditation authority is the Secretary—the amount provided for by the regulations, or
in any other case—the amount required by the accreditation authority.
The accreditation authority may, on application, grant or refuse appointment as a biosecurity auditor.
The accreditation authority may refuse appointment as a biosecurity auditor—
if the application for appointment does not comply with a requirement imposed by or under this Act, or

if the accreditation authority is not satisfied that the applicant can ensure that the conduct of biosecurity audits by the applicant will be carried out only by individuals who are suitable and have the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required by the accreditation authority’s appointment policy, or
if the accreditation authority is of the opinion that the applicant is not a suitable person to be appointed as a biosecurity auditor, or
on any other grounds prescribed by the regulations.
A decision about the suitability of a person for appointment may be made having regard to any of the following—
the fact that the applicant has been found guilty of an offence under this Act or the regulations, or an offence under any other Act or law,
an accreditation audit,
any other matter prescribed by the regulations,
any other circumstances that the accreditation authority considers relevant.
The accreditation authority is to give the applicant notice in writing of a decision to grant or refuse appointment.

An accreditation authority that fails to give an applicant for appointment notice of a decision to grant or refuse appointment within the period prescribed by the regulations is taken to have refused appointment.

An appointment as a biosecurity auditor that is made under this Part remains in force for a period (not exceeding 5 years) specified by the accreditation authority in any notice by which appointment is granted or renewed, unless sooner cancelled.
The appointment has no effect during any period in which the appointment is suspended.

The responsible accreditation authority may, at any time, by notice in writing to a person who has been appointed as a biosecurity auditor, vary the appointment of the person (including any conditions of appointment imposed by an accreditation authority).
A variation includes the imposition of new conditions on an appointment, the substitution of a condition, or the omission or amendment of a condition.
The regulations may make further provision for the variation of an appointment, including—
applications for variation, and
fees for applications for variation.
A biosecurity auditor may apply to an accreditation authority for renewal of appointment as a biosecurity auditor.
An application must—
be in a form approved by the accreditation authority, and
include or be accompanied by any information or evidence of a kind prescribed by the regulations, and
include or be accompanied by any other information or evidence that the accreditation authority reasonably requires to assess the application.
The accreditation authority may require a fee to be paid for an application for renewal of appointment.
The accreditation authority may require the application fee to accompany the application.
The amount of the application fee is—
if the accreditation authority is the Secretary—the amount provided for by the regulations, or
in any other case—the amount required by the accreditation authority.

If an application for renewal of appointment as a biosecurity auditor is duly made to the responsible accreditation authority before the expiry of the appointment, the appointment is taken to continue in force until the accreditation authority notifies the applicant of a decision to grant or refuse the application.

heading.b: Grant or refusal of renewal application

block.txt: An accreditation authority may, on application, renew or refuse to renew appointment as a biosecurity auditor.
An accreditation authority may refuse to renew appointment as a biosecurity auditor—
if the application for renewal of appointment does not comply with any requirement imposed by or under this Act, or

if the accreditation authority is not satisfied that the applicant can ensure that the conduct of biosecurity audits by the applicant will be carried out only by individuals who are suitable and have the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required by the accreditation authority’s appointment policy, or
if the accreditation authority is of the opinion that the applicant is not a suitable person to be appointed as a biosecurity auditor, or
on any grounds prescribed by the regulations.
A decision about the suitability of a person for appointment may be made having regard to any of the following—
the fact that the applicant has been found guilty of an offence under this Act or the regulations, or an offence under any other Act or law,
any biosecurity audit relating to the person,
any other matter prescribed by the regulations,
any other circumstances that the accreditation authority considers relevant.
An accreditation authority is to give the applicant notice in writing of a decision to grant or refuse renewal of appointment as a biosecurity auditor.

An accreditation authority that fails to give an applicant for renewal of appointment as a biosecurity auditor notice of a decision to grant or refuse the application within the period prescribed by the regulations is taken to have refused to renew the appointment.

heading.b: Conditions of appointment as biosecurity auditor

block.txt: Appointment as a biosecurity auditor is subject to the following conditions—
any conditions prescribed by the regulations,
any conditions imposed by the responsible accreditation authority.
The responsible accreditation authority may impose conditions on appointment as a biosecurity auditor—
at the time of the appointment or renewal of appointment, or
at any other time by variation to the appointment.

heading.b: Condition that work be carried out only by individuals

block.txt: It is a condition of appointment as a biosecurity auditor that the conduct of biosecurity audits by the biosecurity auditor will be carried out only by an individual—
with the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required by the responsible accreditation authority’s appointment policy, and
who is the biosecurity auditor or an identified individual with respect to the conduct of biosecurity audits by the biosecurity auditor.

heading.b: Grounds for suspension or cancellation of appointment

block.txt: Each of the following constitutes grounds for suspending or cancelling appointment as a biosecurity auditor—
the accreditation authority is of the opinion that the biosecurity auditor has contravened a requirement imposed by or under this Act,

the accreditation authority is not satisfied that the biosecurity auditor can ensure that the conduct of biosecurity audits by the biosecurity auditor will be carried out only by individuals who are suitable and have the qualifications, skills, knowledge and experience required by the accreditation authority’s appointment policy,
the accreditation authority is of the opinion that the biosecurity auditor is not a suitable person to be appointed as a biosecurity auditor,

the accreditation authority receives information about the biosecurity auditor and the accreditation authority is of the opinion that, had the information been received at the time when the application for appointment or renewal of the appointment was made, it would have refused the application,
any other grounds prescribed by the regulations.
A decision about the suitability of a person for appointment may be made having regard to any of the following—
the fact that the biosecurity auditor has been found guilty of an offence under this Act or the regulations, or an offence under any other Act or law,
a biosecurity audit in relation to the biosecurity auditor,
any matter prescribed by the regulations,
any other circumstances that the accreditation authority considers relevant.
In this Division—
biosecurity auditor includes a former biosecurity auditor.

The responsible accreditation authority may, by notice in writing to a biosecurity auditor, suspend the appointment of the biosecurity auditor if there are grounds for the suspension of the appointment.
The regulations may prescribe circumstances in which it is mandatory for the responsible accreditation authority to suspend the appointment of a biosecurity auditor.
A responsible accreditation authority must suspend the appointment of a biosecurity auditor if it is mandatory for the accreditation authority to suspend the appointment.
Notice of the suspension must specify—
the date or time from which the suspension takes effect, and
the period of suspension, and
the grounds for the suspension.

heading.b: Biosecurity auditor to be given opportunity to make submissions about suspension

block.txt: Before suspending the appointment of a biosecurity auditor, an accreditation authority must—
give notice in writing to the biosecurity auditor of the accreditation authority’s intention to suspend the appointment and the proposed grounds for doing so, and
invite the biosecurity auditor to make a submission to the accreditation authority about the proposed suspension, and
take into account any submission made to the accreditation authority by the biosecurity auditor before the deadline for the making of a submission.

An accreditation authority is to specify a deadline for the making of a submission to the accreditation authority about the proposed suspension that is at least 30 days after notice of the proposed suspension is given to the biosecurity auditor.
The responsible accreditation authority may, by notice in writing to a biosecurity auditor, cancel the appointment of the biosecurity auditor if—
the responsible accreditation authority is satisfied that there are grounds for the cancellation of the appointment, or
the biosecurity auditor applies for cancellation of the appointment.
The regulations may prescribe circumstances in which it is mandatory for the responsible accreditation authority to cancel the appointment of a biosecurity auditor.
A responsible accreditation authority must cancel the appointment of a biosecurity auditor if it is mandatory for the accreditation authority to cancel the appointment.
Notice of the cancellation must specify—
the date or time from which cancellation takes effect, and
the grounds for the cancellation.

heading.b: Biosecurity auditor to be given opportunity to make submissions about cancellation

block.txt: Before cancelling the appointment of a biosecurity auditor, an accreditation authority must—
give notice in writing to the biosecurity auditor of the accreditation authority’s intention to cancel the appointment and the proposed grounds for doing so, and
invite the biosecurity auditor to make a submission to the accreditation authority about the proposed cancellation, and
take into account any submission made to the accreditation authority by the biosecurity auditor before the deadline for the making of a submission.

The accreditation authority must specify a deadline for the making of a submission to the accreditation authority about the proposed cancellation that is at least 30 days after notice of the proposed cancellation is given to the biosecurity auditor.
An accreditation authority is not required to give notice under this section of a proposed cancellation if—
the appointment of the biosecurity auditor is suspended, or
the biosecurity auditor has applied for cancellation of the appointment.

heading.b: Effect of suspension or cancellation on conditions

block.txt: Appointment as a biosecurity auditor may be suspended or cancelled unconditionally or subject to such conditions as the accreditation authority imposes.
Those conditions may include (but are not limited to) any conditions to which the appointment was subject immediately before it was suspended or cancelled.

The accreditation authority may, by notice in writing given to the former biosecurity auditor, attach new conditions to, or vary or revoke any existing conditions of, the suspension or cancellation of the appointment.

heading.b: Offence of contravening conditions of appointment

block.txt: A biosecurity auditor or former biosecurity auditor who contravenes a condition of appointment imposed by or under this Part is guilty of an offence.
An offence against this section is a category 2 offence.
An offence against this section is an executive liability offence.
A person who is guilty of an offence against this section because the person contravenes a requirement of a condition of appointment to do or refrain from doing something—
continues, until the requirement is complied with and despite the fact that any specified period or time for compliance has expired or passed, to be liable to comply with the requirement, and
is guilty of a continuing offence for each day the contravention continues.
Subsection (3) does not apply to the extent that a requirement of a condition is revoked.
A person who impersonates a biosecurity auditor is guilty of an offence.
